description: EXAMPLE site copy of upload_rules.json used with examples/upload: names the invented listing procedure MY_DIR_LIST_PROC.

status.comment: Files a unit WRITES are released only if its status OUT parameter says success at exit (first alias found; two matches = REVIEW_REQUIRED). No status parameter = always released.

open_handles_at_end.comment: units_without_fclose: unit never calls FCLOSE/FCLOSE_ALL, so legacy files were closed at session end with full content -> submit. units_with_fclose: a handle still open at exit was not closed on that path -> discard (confirmed rule).

metadata.comment: Optional values stored with every output file. business_date_aliases: first IN parameter found is passed as p_business_date. context_parameters: IN parameters packed as NAME=value; into p_context. DATE/TIMESTAMP parameters are converted with date_format.

session.comment: Each upload unit gets this IN parameter if it has none; USERENV('SESSIONID') and SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','SESSIONID') are replaced by it. It is passed to BEGIN_UNIT as the load id of the input files (ORAAS_FILE_IN.LOAD_ID). Set "session": null to disable.

mark_on_close.comment: After every FCLOSE of a file opened in read mode, oraas_utl.mark_input(file, session, flag, unit) is added. FCLOSE inside an exception handler other than NO_DATA_FOUND = failure_flag; elsewhere the flag is decided at run time from the status parameter and error-flag variables. The last mark for a load wins, so a later move to the error folder still ends as 'E'. scope: all | units_without_move.

_comment_frame_trigger_calls: Names of your legacy directory-listing procedure(s). Units calling them get a frame even without UTL_FILE, so the replacement (plsql/adapters/listing_procedure_template.sql) knows the unit.

interface_overrides.comment: Unit name (e.g. PKG.PROC) -> INTERFACE_CODE used in ORAAS_FILE_IN, when not the unit name.

_comment_site_names: manual_markers: objects whose presence means a unit was already migrated by hand (e.g. your hand-off procedure or raw upload table). shared_objects: definitions of those objects, never converted. Both empty by default; fill them with YOUR names in a private copy of this file.

directory_dependencies.comment: These need an Oracle directory object and do not work on ORAAS. They are outside the UTL_FILE shim, so the unit is sent to review.
